searchText: Hey all, should these items have the same ssz marshalings? ```go blk := &block{ Slot: 5, Body: nil, } blk2 := &block{ Slot: 5, Body: &blockBody{}, } ``` SSZ doesn't have a notion of `nil` object other than an instantiation of an object filled entirely with default values for each field. Empty `blockBody` would represent an actual `blockBody` with default values for all fields So if your parser fills `nil` with an empty blockBody, then it would be the same, otherwise I'd say the top is undefined ah great <@291925846556540928> so every time we see a nil we should treat it as instantiates object of a type with 0 values the opposite, treating an object full of 0 values as nil seems wrong and incorrect, right? See `nil` in what context? We don't have any `nil` in the spec or tests You could llocally decide that is what it means internally, but not entirely sure what the value would be there So in Go if we just do something like ``` blk := &block{ Slot: 5, } ``` > the opposite, treating an object full of 0 values as nil seems wrong and incorrect, right? Yes, an object full of zero values is actually an object and not `nil` so I wouldn't treat it as such the rest of the fields will be treated as `nil` in Go but we should just treat them as instantiated, zero-valued items then I see. If the `block` is known as an SSZ type, then you would want to instantiate it with the default values of the unspecified fields great that clarifies things, thanks so much Danny if you are following the way we use defaults in the spec. Otherwise, you'd want to be verbose and explicitly instantiate those nil fields yeah, no problem

excerpts.content:
SSZ doesn't have a notion of `nil` object other than an instantiation of an object filled entirely with default values for each field.
Empty `blockBody` would represent an actual `blockBody` with default values for all fields

So if your parser fills `nil` with an empty blockBody, then it would be the same, otherwise I'd say the top is undefined
